clue.text: Doctor touring Fife, lost and annoyed

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so the place name's letters wander into a new order
to tour a place is to go all the way round it, so the doctor surrounds the other letters

parts.note: MD is the abbreviation for a Doctor of Medicine
the Scottish county's letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor on a tour of Fife gets lost and is irritated about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Fife is a county in eastern Scotland. The scrambled county sits between the M and D of the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Miffed is an informal synonym for slightly offended or put out.

clue.text: Clergyman, one entering large church

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the single letter goes into the church word

parts.note: a minster is a large or important church, such as York Minster
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A clergyman walks into a great church.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a member of the clergy, especially in Protestant churches.

clue.text: Dance enthusiast circling with energy

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the first letter of the short word goes round to its end

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
and means together with
go means energy or vigour, as in 'full of go'

explanation.surface: A keen dancer whirls round full of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circling' seems to describe the dancer spinning, but it tells you to rotate the word for 'with' so its front letter goes to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish courtship dance in triple time.

clue.text: Greek character held by secret agent

indicators.note: held by says the answer is gripped inside the following words, spanning a word gap

parts.note: the end of secret and the start of agent

explanation.surface: A Greek is detained by a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet, so a character in the writing sense.

clue.text: Awful wretch pocketing it for a bird-watcher

indicators.note: something awful is in a bad state, so the word after it is badly jumbled
to pocket something is to put it inside, so the jumbled word holds the short one

parts.note: the letters of wretch rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadful scoundrel steals something from a birder.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitcher is a keen birder who travels to see rare species, a slang term from British birding.

clue.text: About to appear beneath Ward, late male comic writer

indicators.note: comic means funny or absurd, so the preceding words are played about with
in a down entry, beneath means coming after, so the short piece goes at the bottom

parts.note: the letters of these three words rearranged
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A dead man named Ward was a funny writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic writer' reads as one phrase, but comic is the anagram signal and writer alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter de la Mare was an English poet and novelist, author of The Listeners.

clue.text: One may be seen by the roadside, clue lending support to illegal trading

definitions.text: One may be seen by the roadside

indicators.note: in a down entry, the piece that supports another sits below it, so it comes second

parts.note: to traffic is to deal illegally, as in drugs
a sign is a clue or indication

explanation.surface: A hint supports some illicit dealing, perhaps spotted at the side of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic signs are the boards giving directions and warnings that stand beside roads.

clue.text: Try ringing the Parisian therapist

indicators.note: ringing means forming a ring round, so the verb surrounds the French word

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Try calling the therapist from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringing' looks like telephoning; it means encircling. Try is the courtroom sense, as a judge tries a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A healer is someone who cures, a looser word for a therapist.

clue.text: Occupy a place on bank

parts.note: re means on the subject of
a river's bank is its side

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a spot on a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to live in or inhabit a place, which is to occupy it.

clue.text: Relax? One might after a row

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for easing off after effort
second meaning: what a rower literally does when the stroke is done

explanation.walkthrough: Row reads first as a quarrel (rhyming with cow); it is the boating sense (rhyming with go).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stop working for a while, taken from rowers pausing with their blades out of the water.

clue.text: A sugar-coated chocolate drop having no equal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sweet of chocolate covered in hundreds and thousands

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as praise for one sweet, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: From French for unequalled, the word is both an adjective for peerless and the name of a small chocolate disc topped with sprinkles.

clue.text: Accumulate a large amount

parts.note: taken as written
a mass is a large quantity

explanation.surface: Gather a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather together or pile up over time.

clue.text: Miss O'Hara appearing briefly in brilliant red

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Scarlett O'Hara is the heroine of Gone with the Wind

explanation.surface: Scarlett O'Hara makes a short appearance dressed in vivid red.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a bright red colour with a slight orange tinge.

clue.text: Party for church workers

parts.note: Labour is a major British political party
taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A political party courting churchgoing working people.
explanation.definitionFit: A labour force is the body of people available for work, a collective term for workers.

clue.text: Strange life in section of London borough

indicators.note: in places the jumbled word inside the next piece
strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the next word is put into an odd order

parts.note: the letters of life rearranged
an end is a part or section, as in the business end

explanation.surface: Odd lives being led in a part of a London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Section of London borough' reads as one phrase; section is wordplay and of is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Enfield is a borough on the northern edge of Greater London.

clue.text: Urges Ben — 'order a snack'

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
taken as written
an edict is an official order

explanation.surface: Someone presses Ben to place an order for a light meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order a snack' sounds like an instruction at a café; order is the wordplay for the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs Benedict, poached eggs and ham on a muffin with hollandaise, is a brunch dish, here called a snack.

clue.text: Round plug, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: shaped like a circle
second meaning: a leaflet sent out to many, which may advertise something

explanation.walkthrough: A round plug suggests an electrical fitting; a plug is also a piece of publicity, which a mailed leaflet can be.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for round and a noun for a printed notice distributed widely, such as an advertisement.

clue.text: Fit to be eaten at home? Salt needs to be added

parts.note: being in means being at home
to season food is to add salt to it

explanation.surface: A home cook tastes a dish and decides it needs more salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is in season is currently available and at its best, ready for eating.

clue.text: What one may experience driving under the Mersey?

definitions.text: What one may experience driving under the Mersey?

parts.words: What one may experience driving under the Mersey?
parts.note: surface reading: the view a motorist gets inside the road tunnels beneath the river at Liverpool
setter's reading: a narrowing of sight to a small central field, or a narrow single-minded outlook

explanation.walkthrough: The Mersey is the river at Liverpool, crossed by road tunnels; the phrase literally describes what a driver sees there.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a condition of seeing only straight ahead, and figuratively a blinkered focus.

clue.text: In the end, book of maps should be printed on time

indicators.note: in a down entry, something printed on top comes first, so the book precedes the next piece

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Eventually, the map book should be printed punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: At last means finally, after a long wait.

clue.text: Song about sailor leaving peninsula

indicators.note: about means around, so the song is placed round the sailor

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
AB stands for able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A song about a sailor departing from a stretch of coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving' looks like a deletion signal but only links the wordplay to the definition; nothing is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabia is the large peninsula of south-west Asia between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: Lists of charges resulting from arguments about a right

indicators.note: about means around, so the quarrels go round the other pieces

parts.note: tiffs are petty quarrels
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Price lists come out of disputes over an entitlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a schedule of prices or duties, so tariffs are lists of charges.

clue.text: Eyeglass found by spy, worn by evil doctor on cape

indicators.note: clothes worn by someone wrap around them, so the spy goes round the following pieces

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted within an organisation

indicators.note: in an across entry, one piece set on another is placed directly before it

parts.note: Dr No is the villain of the James Bond novel and film
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A spy and a Bond villain in a cloak share a single lens.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the Bond world it evokes is full of monocled villains.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle is a single lens worn in one eye, an old word for which is eyeglass.

clue.text: Colour of bream, swimming

indicators.note: a swimming fish moves about, so the fish's letters move about too

parts.note: the fish, taken as written

explanation.surface: The colour of a bream as it swims.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is a yellowish-orange colour, named after fossil resin.

clue.text: Pairs cool off in citadel

indicators.note: off means gone bad or not right, so the preceding letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Couples cool down inside a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool off' reads as one phrase; off is the anagram signal and cool is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis is the fortified high part of an ancient Greek city, a citadel.

clue.text: Most of fruit and veg

indicators.note: most of means all but a little, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: The bulk of the fruit and vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit and veg' reads as one stock phrase; fruit is wordplay and veg alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The pea is a green seed eaten as a vegetable; veg is short for vegetable.

clue.text: Cross, dramatist at rear of theatre

parts.note: Ben Travers wrote the Aldwych farces of the 1920s

indicators.note: the rear of something is its back end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of theatre

explanation.surface: An angry playwright stands at the back of the auditorium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry; it is the verb meaning to go across. Ben Travers was an English farce writer.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across or through, so it means to cross.

clue.text: Caution shown crossing over a densely populated district

indicators.note: a path crossing something spans it from side to side, so one word stretches around the other

parts.note: to caution is to warn
re means concerning, as over does in 'argue over'

explanation.surface: A warning is given about crossing a crowded neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like a reversal signal, but here it means about or concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: A warren is a crowded maze of streets or buildings, by analogy with a rabbit warren.
